mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1pp, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings potential, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE > 5.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 0.5% signals a weakening consumer sector, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and RSAFS decline > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 0.5% MoM, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic slowdown and reduced corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher quarterly growth rate in real GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic momentum and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters when GDPC1 growth is above 2.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals rising inflation and monetary tightening expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL MoM change > 2.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of slow payroll growth (PAYEMS MoM growth < 0.5%) and rising unemployment (UNRATE MoM increase > 0.1%) signals labor market deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS MoM growth < 0.5% and UNRATE MoM increase > 0.1%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS MoM growth < 0.5% and UNRATE MoM increase > 0.1%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-housing boom regime, a month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals reduced consumer confidence and economic uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In post-housing boom periods, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
